curriculumDefinition.commandsAndConcepts: `:`; addresses `.`, `$`, numbers, marks, search addresses; `%`; ranges with `,` and `;`; offsets; visual range `'<,'>`; `:delete`, `:yank`, `:put`, `:copy`/`:t`, `:move`/`:m`, `:join`, `:sort` with the `n`, `u`, and `/pat/` flags; safe undo and preview habits
curriculumDefinition.learningOutcome: Read and construct a range, then apply a deterministic line operation to it
curriculumDefinition.representativeExercises: Move a helper below another function; copy a fixture; delete matching line numbers; sort selected imports; join a range
curriculumDefinition.priorityAndPortability: Core automation. Command availability and undo grouping can vary in reimplementations, so the app defines and tests its supported behavior

lessons.title: Address the line set
lessons.objective: Use current, final, numeric, and whole-buffer addresses before an Ex command.

activities.title: An Ex command can start with a line address
activities.body: In an Ex command, an optional address or range chooses the lines before the action runs. `.` means the current line, `$` the last line, a number one line, and `%` the whole file.
activities.contrast: Without an address, a line command starts from the current line.

lessons.title: Join and sort ranges
lessons.objective: Transform complete line sets with deterministic join and sort operations.

activities.title: Join or sort a selected range of lines
activities.body: `:join` combines the addressed lines and cleans up spacing. `:sort` orders them, and `:sort!` reverses that order. Flags change what is compared: `n` sorts on the first number in each line, `u` keeps only one of each identical line, and `/pat/` sorts on the text that follows the match. Use a narrow range to protect unrelated lines.
activities.contrast: `J` is local; Ex ranges make a multi-line boundary explicit.

activities.title: Address first, operate second
activities.body: You can now construct deterministic line operations from numeric, current, final, mark, search, whole-buffer, and visual addresses. Keep the range narrow, predict it before Enter, inspect the result, and undo a wrong prediction.
takeaways: `,` keeps original context; `;` makes the left endpoint temporary current context.
Delete, yank, and put interact with registers; copy and move do not yank.
Join and sort transform an explicit line set.
Marks, searches, and visual ranges are more durable than memorized numbers.

reference.purpose: Address current, final, numbered, or all lines.

reference.purpose: Address lines through marks or searches.

Join or order an addressed line set.
notes: Sort bang reverses order in these lessons.

reference.purpose: Use the first and last Visual selection lines.
